subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should OpenClaw support only a workspace-scoped file manager, also add a system filesystem scope, or keep Mission Control limited to bootstrap agent files for now?
rationale: The code path is a Gateway/UI file-access boundary and the issue asks to broaden read/write reach beyond the existing allowlist, so automation cannot choose the permanent security posture or product scope.

options.title: Approve Workspace-Only API
options.body: Keep system files out of scope and finish a bounded `agents.workspace.*` design with explicit limits, root containment, scopes, and proof.

options.title: Design System Scope Separately
options.body: Keep this issue open as a product/security design item for a host filesystem browser with explicit operator controls and audit behavior.

options.title: Retain Bootstrap Files Only
options.body: Decline the broader browser and keep the current allowlisted Mission Control file panel as the supported core surface.

recommendation.title: Approve Workspace-Only API
recommendation.body: Keep system files out of scope and finish a bounded `agents.workspace.*` design with explicit limits, root containment, scopes, and proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses Gateway protocol shape, Control UI ergonomics, and fs-safe security boundaries where recent history points to this owner path.
